bib.title: MERLOT: Multimodal Neural Script Knowledge Models

read.skipped: Reference list skimmed; long token/attention-weight dumps in Figures 5, 6, 11 scanned only.

question: Can a model learn commonsense, temporal multimodal script knowledge from unlabeled YouTube videos with ASR transcripts, and does it transfer to video QA and static-image reasoning?
hypothesis: Pretraining on diverse videos with both frame-level and video-level objectives yields representations of events over time that beat models trained on static image-caption pairs.
contributions: MERLOT, an end-to-end vision and language model that learns multimodal world representations from videos and their transcripts, using no labeled data
YT-Temporal-180M, a diverse corpus of frames/ASR derived from a filtered set of 6M YouTube videos
Experiments/ablations on 14 tasks spanning finetuning and zero-shot transfer, images and videos

method.summary: A ResNet-50 + 12-layer ViT image encoder (from scratch) and a RoBERTa-base-initialised 12-layer joint transformer are pretrained on 180M (frame, 32-BPE-token ASR segment) pairs from 6M YouTube videos with three objectives: contrastive frame-transcript matching, attention-masked language modelling, and temporal frame reordering. The model is then finetuned per task with a 2-layer MLP head on the CLS token, or used zero-shot for story ordering.
method.task: self-supervised video+language pretraining; transfer to video QA and VCR

datasets.name: YT-Temporal-180M
datasets.size: 6M videos, 180M segments, 5B BPE tokens of ASR
datasets.source: 27M candidate YouTube video IDs (18 FreeBase topic pages, VLOG, HowTo100M, MSCOCO-noun searches, BFS over 50k channels); released as video IDs only
datasets.preprocessing: drop videos with no English ASR, >20 min, Gaming, thumbnails with <4 COCO objects at 30% prob or mean cosine sim >0.9; ASR denoised by GROVER-Large seq2seq (perplexity >200 drops video); segments of L=32 BPE tokens, middle frame; 16 segments per example

datasets.name: VCR
datasets.preprocessing: bounding boxes drawn as coloured highlights in pixel space

datasets.name: LSMDC (FiB, MC) and MSRVTT-MC
datasets.size: LSMDC-FiB test 30,000 examples from 10,000 clips; MSRVTT-MC 2,990 questions; LSMDC-MC 100,000 train pairs created
datasets.source: Rohrbach et al.; Yu et al. 2018

models.name: MERLOT
models.architecture: ResNet-50 (C5 removed, 2x2 avg-pool) + 12-layer 768-d ViT image encoder; 12-layer 768-d joint transformer (RoBERTa base)
models.init_from: image encoder random init; joint encoder and word embeddings from RoBERTa
models.context: pretraining: language-only 512 tokens (16x32); joint encoder 396 tokens (4 segments, 192x352)

other.image_encoder_flops: 40 gigaFLOPs per forward, 2% of 2 teraFLOPs for Faster-RCNN

other.denoise_data: RealNews trimmed to 600 BPE tokens; lowercase, no punct, 1% word replacement (25% homophone via CMUdict, 75% random BPE), 1% filler insertion

models.name: CLIP, UNITER, ViLBERT, VILLA, ERNIE-ViL, etc.

training.objective: contrastive frame-transcript matching (tau=0.05, weight 0.25) + attention-masked LM (20% of tokens corrupted; 50% random token, 50% one of top-20% attended tokens; SpanBERT spans avg 0.5 tokens each side) + temporal reordering (40% of the time scramble i in [2,N] frames; two-layer MLP on pairs of frame CLS states, cross-entropy)
training.seq_len: N=16 segments x L=32 BPE (512 tokens language-only); joint encoder 4 groups of N=4, 396 tokens
training.regularisation: image augmentation: random scale 1.125-1.5x and crop, brightness/contrast jitter 0.7-1.3 on 80% of images; random choice of clean or noisy ASR per iteration

other.finetune: AdamW beta2 0.98, lr 1.2e-5 (searched [1e-5,2e-4] on VCR), weight decay 0.01, dropout 10%, linear warmup 10% then linear decay to 0, early stopping each epoch, 18 epochs default, batch 64 (16 for MSRVTT-QA/TGIF/ActivityNet/LSMDC/MSRVTT-MC); per-task steps in Table 8 (VCR 60k, TGIF 70k, LSMDC-FiB 150k, ActivityNetQA 34k, DramaQA 3.5k in text vs 18k in table)
other.story_ordering: extra 10 epochs pretraining, peak lr 2e-5, 384x384, 5 segments, caption-frame temporal loss with 4 options

inference.samples: story ordering: 2 random orderings of unknown-position embeddings averaged; finetuned results single reported number, no seeds stated
inference.prompting: no prompting; video frames sampled uniformly (5 to 7 frames per clip), question and answers concatenated (QSEP separator in TGIF/LSMDC)

other.story_score: sum over caption/frame pairs of log pairwise probability; CLIP/UNITER use Hungarian maximum-weight bipartite matching

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction correct for QA/multiple choice; VCR Q->AR requires both answer and rationale right

metrics.name: Spearman
metrics.definition: rank correlation of predicted vs true story order

eval.protocol: standard splits; ablations on VCR Q->A and TVQA+ validation; no seeds or significance tests stated

availability.data: video IDs and transcripts only, not videos

evidence.quote: This pretraining process on this hardware takes 30 hours.

limits: Frame ordering is a coarse temporal objective; finer temporal localisation in transcripts is future work (Sec 5)
English-only YouTube; multilingual learning left open
Temporal ordering loss helps TVQA but slightly hurts VCR (75.5 without vs 75.2 with); authors say it is mainly a query interface
Linear-probe action recognition trails CLIP (Table 6); benchmark object/background bias cited
Dataset skewed: ~30% local broadcast news, crime topics, YouTube popularity biases; authors do not advocate deployed use
Pretraining performance had not plateaued at 40 epochs; no compute scaling beyond that tested
Only video IDs released, so exact reproduction of the corpus is hard
No seeds or variance reported; ablation accuracy differences of ~1 point are single runs
Models are base-size only; 2021 baselines have since been superseded

terms.definition: knowledge of how events unfold over time (before, present, after), after Schank and Abelson 1975
mask highly attended-to tokens from a language-only encoder 50% of the time, as a proxy for visually grounded words
